title: Solving a separable equation
intro: From an equation of change to the one curve a system actually follows.
prompt: Drag into order — the first step at the top.

steps.text: Read the order, and check whether degree is even defined
Gather every y with dy on one side, every x with dx on the other
Integrate both sides — one constant of integration is enough
Rearrange into the general solution, carrying its arbitrary constant
Apply the initial condition to solve for that constant
Substitute the particular solution back; the residual must be exactly zero

debrief:
Reading the equation **first** is not ceremony. Order tells you how many conditions you will need before you go looking for them, and if the equation turns out not to be separable, you have learned that before investing in the attempt rather than after.

The pairing in the middle is the heart of it: integrating gives a **family**, and the initial condition selects the **member**. `dy/dx = -2xy` separates to `dy/y = -2x dx` and integrates to the Gaussian family `y = C·e^(-x²)`; y(0) = 10 makes it `y = 10·e^(-x²)`. Stop at the general solution and you have described what is possible, not what will happen — which is exactly the failure in this pack's thermal-model case.

The last step is the cheapest insurance in the whole workflow. Substitution is mechanical, takes seconds, and a wrong answer leaves a residual that is loud rather than subtle. Verifying is faster than wondering.
